reviews.title: Closure notices only in Turkish: misleading for tourists
reviews.text:
The app has an English interface, but important notices are shown only in Turkish. For example, on the Perge Archaeological Site page, the note that the ancient theatre is temporarily closed for restoration appears only in Turkish. I only found out because I translated it myself, after I had already planned my trip around seeing the theatre.

The same problem affects ticket info. The ticket screen shows a green "MüzeKart is valid" label in English, while the Turkish note above it says the MüzeKart is valid for Turkish citizens only. As a foreign visitor, I couldn't tell if the card applied to me

reviews.title: I Should’ve Listened to the Reviews 😂
reviews.text:
I read all the reviews saying this app was basically useless for foreign visitors, but I decided to be optimistic. That was my first mistake. 😂

I first tried purchasing tickets through the official website using multiple credit cards from multiple banks. Nothing worked. So, thinking the app might work better, I actually downloaded it specifically to try purchasing my tickets there. Spoiler alert: it did not.

The app wouldn’t even let me change the quantity of tickets I wanted to purchase. At one point I was so committed to making this work that I said, “Fine, I’ll buy ONE ticket at a time.” Still declined. 😂

I have rarely worked this hard to give someone my money.

If an international tourist is trying to purchase tickets to visit Türkiye’s museums, accepting international credit cards and allowing us to select the number of tickets feels like a pretty reasonable starting point.

One star for consistency, though, the bad reviews were completely accurate.
